title: Find a Number's Position
description:
Given an array `nums` and a number `target`, return the position (index) where `target` first appears.

If `target` isn't in the array, return `-1`.

Example: for `nums = [4, 8, 15]` and `target = 8`, return `1`, because `nums[1]` is 8.
hints: Concept: this is called a linear search. You check each element one at a time, from the start, until you find what you're looking for.
Approach: loop through the positions. As soon as `nums[i]` equals `target`, you've found the first one, so return `i` right away. If the loop finishes without finding it, it isn't there.

workedExample.title: Does the Array Contain a Negative?
workedExample.description: Return `true` if any number in `nums` is below zero, otherwise `false`.
workedExample.explanation:
`return` inside a loop ends the method immediately, so there's no need to keep looking once the answer is known.

The `return false` after the loop only runs if the loop checked everything and found nothing. Your problem has the same shape: return early when you find the target, and return a "not found" value after the loop.

walkthrough.note: i = 0: nums[0] is 4. Not 8, keep going.
i = 1: nums[1] is 8. Found it! Return 1 immediately.
If target were 99, the loop would check all three numbers without a match, and you'd return -1 after the loop.

mistakes.hint: You returned -1 as soon as the first number didn't match. Only return -1 after the loop has checked everything.
You returned the last match. Return as soon as you find the first one.
